Ir-shemesh
ir-SHEH-mesh
proper noun
Hebrew Ir-Shemesh, “city of the sun,” a town in the allotment of Dan, akin to Beth-shemesh, “house of the sun.”

📖 Biblical Definition

Ir-shemesh, “the city of the sun,” was a town named in the borders of the inheritance of Dan, set down with Zorah and Eshtaol as the coast of their portion (Jos 19:41). Its name, like that of the neighbouring Beth-shemesh, bears witness to the worship of the sun that the heathen of Canaan practised before Israel possessed the land. The dictionary does not pass the name by, for the Scripture itself warns against the very thing it remembers. Moses charged Israel that they should not lift up their eyes unto heaven, and when they saw the sun, and the moon, and the stars, be driven to worship and serve them, which the LORD had divided unto all nations (Deu 4:19). Israel was to worship not the sun but the Maker of the sun, whose heavens declare His glory (Psa 19:1). And the prophet Malachi turned the very figure to Christ, promising that unto them that fear God’s name the Sun of righteousness should arise with healing in His wings (Mal 4:2). So Ir-shemesh, a city named for the created light, points beyond itself to the uncreated Light, and reproves the folly of bowing to the lamp while forgetting the Lord who lit it.

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

A town of Dan whose name, “city of the sun,” recalls the sun-worship of Canaan and reproves it.

expand to see more

IR-SHEMESH, the “city of the sun,” a town in the allotment of Dan.

It was named with Zorah and Eshtaol in the border of Dan’s inheritance.

Its name, like Beth-shemesh, recalls the sun-worship of the Canaanites.

Israel was forbidden to worship the host of heaven, the work of God’s hand.

The Sun of righteousness, who is Christ, is the true Light the name foreshadows.

📖 Key Scripture

Jos 19:41 — "And the coast of their inheritance was Zorah, and Eshtaol, and Irshemesh,"

Deu 4:19 — "And lest thou lift up thine eyes unto heaven, and when thou seest the sun, and the moon, and the stars, even all the host of heaven, shouldest be driven to worship them, and serve them, which the LORD thy God hath divided unto all nations under the whole heaven."

Psa 19:1 — "The heavens declare the glory of God; and the firmament sheweth his handywork."

Mal 4:2 — "But unto you that fear my name shall the Sun of righteousness arise with healing in his wings; and ye shall go forth, and grow up as calves of the stall."

⚠️ Modern Corruption

A place of Scripture, not a contested doctrine; its name reproves the worship of the creature in place of the Creator.

expand to see more

Ir-shemesh has met no redefinition from the present age, but its name preserves the memory of a corruption the Scripture itself condemns, the worship of the sun and the host of heaven. The dictionary records the town that the reader may see how the names of the land bore witness to its old idolatry.

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The principle to recover is that the creature is never to be worshipped in the place of the Creator. The city of the sun is a standing reproof to the folly that bows to the lamp and forgets the Lord who lit it. The heavens declare His glory, but they are not Himself; and the true Light is the Sun of righteousness, who arises with healing for them that fear the name of God.

🔗 Greek & Hebrew Roots

From the Hebrew for “city of the sun,” Ir-shemesh names a Danite town and reproves sun-worship.

expand to see more

Ir-shemesh — Hebrew Ir-Shemesh, “city of the sun.”

Ir signifies a city; shemesh, the sun.

It lay in the border of Dan with Zorah and Eshtaol.

Its name recalls the sun-worship of the Canaanites.

It points beyond the created light to Christ, the Sun of righteousness.

Usage

"Like the city of the sun, the world still worships the creature and forgets the Creator."

"The heavens declare the glory of God, but they are not God, and must not be adored."

"The true Light is the Sun of righteousness, who arises with healing for them that fear His name."
